data.title: Akt/mTOR pathway is a crucial regulator of skeletal muscle hypertrophy and can prevent muscle atrophy in vivo
data.authors: Bodine SC; Stitt TN; Gonzalez M; Kline WO; Stover GL; Bauerlein R; Zlotchenko E; Scrimgeour A; Lawrence JC; Glass DJ; Yancopoulos GD

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Akt/mTOR signalling is necessary and sufficient to drive skeletal-muscle hypertrophy and counteract atrophy in vivo.
data.abstract_excerpt: Skeletal muscles adapt to changes in their workload by regulating fibre size by unknown mechanisms. The roles of two signalling pathways implicated in muscle hypertrophy on the basis of findings in vitro, Akt/mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin) and calcineurin/NFAT (nuclear factor of activated T cells), were investigated in several models of skeletal muscle hypertrophy and atrophy in vivo. The Akt/mTOR pathway was upregulated during hypertrophy and downregulated during muscle atrophy.

extracted_findings.effect: Akt/mTOR is necessary and sufficient for skeletal muscle hypertrophy and prevents atrophy in vivo
